title: Christianity: beliefs and practices
examples: What is the difference between Catholics and Protestants?

explain.say: Christianity is based on the life and teaching of Jesus, a Jewish teacher from Nazareth who lived about 2,000 years ago. With about 2.3 billion followers, it is the largest religion in the world.

draw.label: Bethlehem, Nazareth and Jerusalem in the Gospel stories

explain.say: Christians believe Jesus is the Son of God and the Christ, or Messiah. They believe he was crucified, rose from the dead, and that through him people can be forgiven and close to God.

draw.text: Christ comes from the Greek for anointed one

explain.say: Most Christians believe in the Trinity: one God in three persons, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.
The Christian Bible has two parts. The Old Testament shares the Hebrew scriptures, and the New Testament holds the four Gospels about Jesus, letters to early churches, and more.

items: Old Testament: law, history, prophets, poetry
New Testament: Gospels, Acts, letters, Revelation

faq.a: Easter is the most important Christian festival. It celebrates the belief that Jesus rose from the dead on the third day after his crucifixion on Good Friday. Christians see it as the victory of life and love over death.
The Trinity is the Christian belief that there is one God in three persons: the Father, the Son, who is Jesus, and the Holy Spirit. They are not three gods, but one God known in three ways.
asks: What does Father, Son and Holy Spirit mean?
Do Christians believe in three gods?

faq.a: Jesus was a Jewish teacher from Nazareth who lived about 2,000 years ago. He taught about God's love and kingdom and healed people. Christians believe he is the Son of God who died and rose again.

The Bible is the Christian holy book. The Old Testament holds the Hebrew scriptures, and the New Testament has 27 books, including the four Gospels of Matthew, Mark, Luke and John. Protestant Bibles have 66 books; Catholic and Orthodox Bibles have more.
asks: How many books are in the Bible?

faq.a: Christmas, on 25 December for most churches, celebrates the birth of Jesus in Bethlehem. Many Orthodox Christians celebrate on 7 January because they follow an older calendar. People go to church, sing carols and give gifts.

faq.q: What is the difference between Catholics and Protestants?
faq.a: Catholics are led by the Pope and value both the Bible and Church tradition. Protestants began with the Reformation in 1517, led by reformers like Martin Luther, and stress the Bible as the final authority. Both follow Jesus.

faq.q: What are the main branches of Christianity?
faq.a: The three largest are Catholic, the biggest, with about half of all Christians; Protestant, including Anglicans, Baptists, Methodists, Lutherans and Pentecostals; and Orthodox, strong in Eastern Europe, Greece, Russia and Ethiopia.

Christians gather in church to pray, sing hymns, hear the Bible read and explained in a sermon, and share Holy Communion, bread and wine remembering Jesus' Last Supper. Many churches meet on Sunday, the day of the resurrection.
asks: What do Christians do at church?
Why do Christians go to church on Sunday?

faq.a: Baptism is the ceremony of joining the Christian family, using water as a sign of washing away sin and new life with God. Some churches baptise babies; others baptise people when they are old enough to choose.

Holy Communion, also called the Eucharist, Mass or the Lord's Supper, is when Christians share bread and wine as Jesus did at the Last Supper before his death. Churches understand its meaning in different ways.
asks: Why do Christians eat bread and wine?

faq.q: Why is the cross the symbol of Christianity?
faq.a: The cross recalls Jesus' death by crucifixion. For Christians it is a symbol of God's love and sacrifice, and with the resurrection, of hope. Some crosses are empty to stress the risen Jesus.
Lent is the 40 days before Easter, not counting Sundays, when many Christians pray, fast or give something up, and give to others. It remembers the 40 days Jesus spent fasting in the desert.
asks: Why do Christians give things up for Lent?

faq.q: What did Jesus teach about loving others?
faq.a: Jesus taught that the greatest commandments are to love God with all your heart and to love your neighbour as yourself. In his parable of the Good Samaritan, a neighbour is anyone in need.
asks: What is the Good Samaritan story about?

faq.a: The Pope is the leader of the Catholic Church and the Bishop of Rome. He lives in Vatican City, the smallest country in the world. Orthodox and Protestant Christians have their own leaders and do not follow the Pope.

facts: Christians numbered about 2.3 billion in 2020, about 28.8 percent of the world, the largest religious group (Pew Research).
The New Testament contains 27 books, including the four Gospels.
The split between the Catholic and Orthodox churches is dated to 1054.
The Protestant Reformation is usually dated from 1517, when Martin Luther published his 95 Theses.
Easter is always on a Sunday; its date changes each year, usually falling in March or April.
